bitfield.description: Both MEM_MCU_RST_AND and MEM_MCU_RST have the same functionality but have different polarity (So basically, one of them is redundant) MCU_CFG[0]: '1' - Force cortex reset. '0' - do nothing. MCU_CFG[1]: '0' - Force cortex reset. '1' - do nothing. WSOC M3 Cortex Reset = HW_rst & mem_mcu_reset & ~mem_mcu_reset_and Where HW_rst is the global reset to the WLAN and reset both MAC and PHY with their registers file.

Both MEM_MCU_RST_AND and MEM_MCU_RST have the same functionality but have different polarity (So basically, one of them is redundant) MCU_CFG[0]: '1' - Force cortex reset. '0' - do nothing. MCU_CFG[1]: '0' - Force cortex reset. '1' - do nothing. WSOC M3 Cortex Reset = HW_rst & mem_mcu_reset & ~mem_mcu_reset_and Where HW_rst is the global reset to the WLAN and reset both MAC and PHY with their registers file.
Priority issued to CTX RAM Master Arbiter: 0 - CTX has priority when accessing CTX RAM 1 - OCP IC has priority when accessing CTX RAM
Priority issued to SCR RAM Master Arbiter: 0 - SCR has priority when accessing SCR RAM, then CTX and then OCP IC 1 - CTX has priority when accessing SCR RAM, then SCR and then OCP IC

register.description: Timer 1: An 16bit "2 event" count time Timer. Triggered by either FW or 8 HW maskable signals (rise or fall) Counts either @40M or @1M

bitfield.description: This field set the timer count clock: 0 - 40M 1 - 1M (using usec_stb) Since timer size is 16bit 0 - Count max delay 64K*25ns=1.63msec at resolution of 25ns 1 - Count max delay 64K*1000ns=65.5msec at resolution of 1us
When timer is triggerd it's counter will count up till reaching this value. Then send interrupt according to mask

register.description: Timer 3: An 16bit "Rx timeout" Timer. SET by either FW or up to 4 HW maskable signals (rise or fall) RST by either FW or up to 8 HW maskable signals (rise or fall) Counts @1M to configurable value Two 2 configurable comparators (=exit points). *Upon its expiry, a reset will be performed by one of the executers (M0 or scripter), This is required to recover the system from Rx stuck situations.

bitfield.description: When timer is equal to this field - it set interrupt (depend on timer interrupt mask field)
When timer is equal to this field - it set interrupt (depend on timer interrupt mask field)

register.description: Timer 3 Trigger h/w sources are: timer3_start_hw_sources[ 3:0] = {1'b0,bs_rise,rxtb_bd_pulse,rx_bd}; timer3_stop_hw_sources [ 7:0] = {1'b0,tx_header_rise,rx_suspend_start,rx_stomp,rx_abort,rx_last,bs_fall,rx_ctrl_td_eop}; For Example: setting.. MEM_TIMER3_START_RISE_MASK[3:0] = 0xE; MEM_TIMER3_START_FALL_MASK[3:0] = 0xF; MEM_TIMER3_STOP_RISE_MASK[7:0] = 0xFE; MEM_TIMER3_STOP_FALL_MASK[7:0] = 0xFF; will casue timer trigger @rx_bd rise and Timer Disable @rx_ctrl_td_eop rise.

register.description: Timer 4: An 16bit "Tx timeout" Timer. Counts @1M to configurable value Two 2 configurable comparators (=exit points). *Upon its expiry, a reset will be performed and the next state will be Rx search.

register.description: Timer 4 Trigger h/w sources are: timer4_start_hw_sources[0] = tx_header_rise; timer4_stop_hw_sources [0] = tx_active_fall; timer4_stop_hw_sources [1] = tx_abort_in_progressl; (few cycles) timer4_stop_hw_sources [2] = tx_active_ble_fall; For Example: setting.. MEM_TIMER4_STOP_RISE_MASK[3:0] = 0xE; MEM_TIMER4_STOP_FALL_MASK[3:0] = 0xF; MEM_TIMER4_START_RISE_MASK[3:0] = 0xE; MEM_TIMER4_START_FALL_MASK[3:0] = 0xF; will casue Timer trigger @"tx_header_rise" rise and Timer Disable @"tx_active_fall" rise.
